items.title: ASX falls as banks, tech stocks decline; CSL names new chair
paras: The Sydney Morning Herald logo The Sydney Morning Herald logo Advertisement Updated Business Markets World markets ASX falls as banks, tech stocks decline; CSL names new chair Staff writers Updated October 26, 2026 — 11:10am , first published October 26, 2026 — 5:20am
You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.
Share A A A The Australian sharemarket has declined at the open after oil prices rose over the weekend, ratcheting up pressure on markets across the globe.
The S&P/ASX 200 was down 64.9 points or 0.7 per cent, to 8730.3 in early trade. The Australian dollar was trading at US70.26¢.

Wall Street lost ground on Friday as oil prices hit their highest mark in four years. Bloomberg Financial stocks are weaker across the board, with Commonwealth Bank leading the way for the big four banks with a 2 per cent decline. National Australia Bank lost 1.7 per cent while Westpac and ANZ Bank each shed 1.9 per cent.

Energy stocks advanced after oil prices rose again over the weekend before easing this morning as the US and Iran remained apart on a deal to end months of war. President Donald Trump told Fox News it was “getting to be decision time” on whether he would make a deal with Tehran or “finish it off”. Meanwhile, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said if rationality existed, the US would “not attempt” an attack. Brent crude advanced above $US116 a barrel while West Texas Intermediate rose above $US102. Woodside Energy rose 1.1 per cent, Santos added 1.5 per cent. Among the refiners, Ampol advanced 0.7 per cent and Viva Energy surged 2.9 per cent.

Mining stocks climbed with BHP adding 1.3 per cent, Fortescue rising 1.5 per cent and Rio Tinto edging up 0.1 per cent. Northern Star added 1 per cent and Evolution Mining rose 1.8 per cent as the gold price steadied at about $US4000 ($5690) per ounce.

Technology stocks followed their Wall Street peers lower as WiseTech shed 1.3 per cent, Xero lost 1.9 per cent and TechnologyOne dipped 0.1 per cent but Codan added 0.6 per cent. Embattled AI company NextDC slumped 3 per cent as it announced its chairman Douglas Flynn would stand for re-election at its annual meeting with investors next month but retire once a replacement is in place, and chief executive Craig Scroggie will forfeit millions in bonuses.

Pharmaceutical giant CSL has named its interim chief executive Gordon Naylor as its next chair, replacing Brian McNamee, who will end his decades-long association with the Australian pharmaceutical giant.
Naylor will take over as chair on March 31. He will hand over chief executive duties to Deborah Waterhouse in February.

McNamee, as CEO, helped steer the company’s transformation from a government agency into one of Australia’s largest listed companies, but it has struggled with a string of downgrades over the past year which sent its shares sharply lower. CSL shares were 2 per cent down in early trade.

On Wall Street on Friday, the S&P 500 fell 0.5 per cent as the index posted its second-straight weekly loss. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.2 per cent, and the Nasdaq composite slipped 0.2 per cent after giving up a modest gain.

Several AI-related companies rallied, helping ease some of the impact from the broader market slide. Micron Technology rose 2.5 per cent, Intel gained 1.7 per cent, Microsoft added 0.7 per cent, and Advanced Micro Devices closed 1.7 per cent higher.

The tech sector’s influence is also capable of quickly switching over to a heavy weight. Stocks that have benefited from the frenzy over AI have been swinging over rising worries about their path ahead. Investors are worried about whether their high prices are justified. Many of those companies have been borrowing to fund investments in AI technology and high interest rates are making those loans more expensive.

“Investors appear increasingly focused on the economics of AI, particularly the substantial upfront costs required to build AI infrastructure and the uncertainty around the timing of returns on those investments,” said Angelo Kourkafas, senior global strategist at Edward Jones, in a research note.

The latest round of corporate earnings are being closely watched to help get a better sense of whether those investments are paying off, or might pay off. Several influential AI-related companies report their latest financial results next week, including Google’s parent, Alphabet, along with Microsoft and Amazon.
Industrial companies had some of the biggest losses. Caterpillar fell 2.4 per cent.

American Express slumped 3.7 per cent, one of several financial stocks that lost ground, despite reporting profits for its most recent quarter that beat analysts’ forecasts. The company did announce its first major job cuts in roughly a decade.
JPMorganChase fell 1.5 per cent, Citigroup dropped 1.5 per cent and Capital One Financial slid 1 per cent.
While higher oil prices weighed down much of the market, they helped boost energy companies. Chevron rose 2.9 per cent and ConocoPhillips gained 3.6 per cent.
European markets closed mostly lower. France’s main index fell 0.4 per cent, though yields on French government bonds eased a bit.
Treasury yields in the US edged higher following sharp drops on Thursday. The yield on the 10-year Treasury edged up to 4.99 per cent from 4.96 per cent late on Thursday.

Yields have been rising globally, partly over worries about governments taking on too much debt. Inflation also remains a concern and is stubbornly well above 3 per cent in the US. That prompted the Federal Reserve to raise its benchmark interest rate at its last meeting in an effort to cool inflation.
Wall Street expects the US central bank to hold rates steady at its meeting next week, but is leaning heavily towards another rate hike in December.

Wall Street will also get several big economic updates next week, including the Fed’s preferred measure of inflation. The personal consumption expenditures index, or PCE, is expected to show that inflation rose at a 3.7 per cent rate in September, sharply above the Fed’s 2 per cent target.

paras: Jefferies India has set these upside targets after reviewing the Q2 2026 results of these companies. ( Photo: Representational AI-generated image for educational purposes only ) AI Quick Read Stocks to buy today | Jefferies India stock recommendations today: The Q2FY27 earnings season is in full swing, and various institutions are busy analysing the Q2 results 2026 of the Indian companies. In this regard, Jefferies India has analysed the Q2 results 2026 of Adani Energy Solutions , AU Small Finance Bank , Bharat Petroleum Limited ( BPCL ), and IDFC First Bank . The global investment bank remains bullish on these four shares following the announcement of these companies' Q2 results. However, the latest Jefferies India report has reduced the upside price targets for Adani Energy Solutions, AU Small Finance Bank, and BPCL shares.

Despite reducing the upside price target, the Jefferies India report has predicted 62% upside in this Adani Group share, saying, "We lower our SOTP-based PT to ₹ 1,980 (vs ₹ 2,060) given the EBITDA cut and continue to value AESL’s ex trading business EBITDA at 22x EV/EBITDA Sept 28E (8% disc. to 10-yr avg.). We maintain 5x EV/EBITDA Sept 28E for the trading business EBITDA, which is 12-18% of overall EBITDA, given the sustainable business profitability spread is yet to be ascertained. Trading is 3% of the SOTP value. Downside risks include 1) inability to maintain interest rate and 2) market share loss."
Adani Energy Solutions' share price finished at ₹ 1,220 per share on Friday.

Despite reducing the upside price target, the latest Jefferies India report has predicted 34% upside in AU Small Finance Bank shares, saying, “We lower earnings est by 1-5% to factor higher opex & tighter bancassurance fee norms. We see 23% CAGR in loans and 28% CAGR in profit over FY27-29 (normalised base of FY27), and ROE improving to 15-16%, with upside from strengthening franchise strength with a universal bank license. We make a slight cut in PT to Rs1,250 (from Rs1,270), based on 2.9x Dec-28E adj. PB. AU stays among our top-picks, and we see 25% Cagr compounding here.”
AU Small Finance Bank share price finished at ₹ 932.90 per share on Friday.

The latest Jefferies India report has reduced the upside price target of BPCL shares also, but the global investment bank has remained bullish on the oil PSU stock, saying, “The risk of escalation in the conflict has led to a sharp rally in Brent, hurting the stock. We note BPCL's performance in 1HFY27 has been significantly ahead of its peer HPCL. The stock is trading at a discount to HPCL on a P/B basis despite a superior full-cycle ROE. We see room for significant re-rating in the stock once hostilities conclude. Maintain Buy with PT of Rs380 - at 1.4x Sep-28 P/B.”

The Jeffeires India has given a ‘buy’ tag to AU Small Finance Bank shares, saying, "We raise estimates for FY27 by 8% and 2-3% for FY28-29 & see ROA improving to 1% in FY27; expansion in FY28 is dragged by lower banca fees. Over FY28-29, we expect c.20% growth in loans and stable NIMs, which, along with some operating synergies, should aid the rise in profitability. Bank's CET-I is at 13%, and given growth plans & lower ROE, it may need capital over 12 months. We retain a price target of ₹ 96 based on 1.4x Dec-28E adjusted PB. Buy stays."

items.title: Hegseth warns prediction market bets warp military judgment, endanger troops
paras: Insider predictions Hegseth warns prediction market bets warp military judgment, endanger troops Pentagon memo: Insider trading gives US enemies key intel on military operations.

119 Credit: Getty Images | AFP/Martin Lelievre Credit: Getty Images | AFP/Martin Lelievre Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth issued a memo warning military personnel against using nonpublic information to make bets on prediction markets, saying the wagers could give important clues to enemy countries.

“Do Not Compromise Military Operations for Personal Financial Gain,” said the subject line of an October 20 memo published yesterday by CBS News . Hegseth’s memo was sent to senior Pentagon leadership, Combatant Command leaders, and Defense Department field activity directors.

Our enemies watch movements in these markets. When an American Service member, intelligence professional, or other Department civilian engages in a financial transaction on a military outcome, they create a signal. That signal can be aggregated, correlated, and exploited by hostile foreign intelligence services to anticipate our movements, targets, and timing. The lives of our Service members often depend on the enemy not knowing what is coming. The men and women who carry our flag into harm’s way deserve a Force that protects them—not one that exposes them to the enemy for personal gain.

In April, a US Army soldier was arrested and charged with using confidential information to make $410,000 in Polymarket bets on the timing of the military’s capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro. An August report by the Anti-Corruption Data Collective said the group found 152 suspicious wallets that placed longshot bets on military and defense markets and won a combined $8 million.

Hegseth’s memo said the prohibition applies to “all financial platforms,” including traditional betting services and prediction markets such as Polymarket and Kalshi. Defense Department personnel may not make any financial transaction informed by nonpublic information, regardless of whether that information is classified or unclassified, Hegseth wrote.

“All Department of War personnel are prohibited from engaging in financial transactions using nonpublic information, either directly or indirectly through a third party… Violations may result in administrative, disciplinary, and, where appropriate, criminal action under the Uniform Code of Military Justice and/or applicable federal law,” Hegseth wrote.

The memo said betting on military matters related to a person’s job can warp one’s judgment. “Beyond operational security, financial stakes can warp judgment,” he wrote. “A logistician with money riding on a strike date has an interest in that date. An analyst with a position on an outcome has an interest in that outcome.”
Kalshi and Polymarket both prohibit insider trading. But criminal charges of the sort described by Hegseth are sure to be a bigger deterrent than being banned from the Kalshi or Polymarket platforms.
This was not the first warning issued internally by the Trump administration, The Associated Press wrote yesterday.

“A group of new accounts on Polymarket made highly specific, well-timed bets on whether the US and Iran would reach a ceasefire just before President Donald Trump announced it in April, resulting in hundreds of thousands of dollars in profits for the new customers ,” the AP wrote. “The White House warned staff against using private information to trade on prediction markets the same day the report came out.”
In another incident, a Trump teleprompter aide reportedly made $100,000 on Kalshi by betting on what Trump would say in prepared remarks.

Prediction markets have flourished under the Trump administration’s light-touch approach to regulation. The Trump administration is also trying to stop state governments from regulating the markets, arguing that state laws are preempted by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s exclusive jurisdiction. Courts have reached different conclusions, and state governments want the Supreme Court to uphold their right to impose restrictions on prediction-market gambling.

items.title: Updated Google privacy policy says your Gmail might be used for advertising
paras: An important clarification Updated Google privacy policy says your Gmail might be used for advertising Turning on Personal Intelligence gives the company more data for ad targeting.

85 Credit: Aurich Lawson Credit: Aurich Lawson Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav Using Google’s products and services has always been fundamentally precarious—doing so gives the world’s largest advertising company a lot of juicy personal data. Google has long said it won’t use the sensitive data from products like Gmail, Drive, and Photos for ad personalization, but a change to the company’s privacy policy appears to dismantle that firewall.

On October 16, Google issued an update to its privacy policy , spotted by Android Authority . The ad personalization section used to include a clear limit on data from certain apps. “We don’t show you personalized ads based on your content from Drive, Gmail, or Photos,” the document said. Now, Google has updated it with the following language.

This equivocation opens the door to using data from apps like Gmail and Photos in ads when it’s shared with other Google services, and it just so happens Google has a mechanism for doing that, with Personal Intelligence. The company released Personal Intelligence in early 2026 , allowing users to hand data from multiple apps to Google AI products. The idea is that the added context from your existing data will lead to better AI answers, but it’s also proving to be a privacy minefield.

Personal Intelligence connects your data to the Gemini app but also to features like AI Mode search. While the Gemini app does not currently have ads, you may see sponsored content in AI search tools. Google’s changes to the privacy policy appear to acknowledge that data shared with AI search via Personal Intelligence could, therefore, contribute to ad personalization.
According to Google, this clarification still doesn’t mean ads are “based directly” on your personal data. Here’s the company’s full statement:

“Connecting your apps is entirely opt-in. Ads will continue to be relevant to things like your query, the context of the response and your interests. Ads will not be based directly on your Gmail inbox or Photos library, and as always, sensitive information will not be used to tailor ads.”

Google’s statement is essentially a roundabout way of confirming that Workspace and Photos data may inform ads. If you interact with AI Mode while Personal Intelligence is enabled, there’s a chance that summaries and insights from your data will inform the answers you get. Because that same data is used for ad targeting, it’s accurate to say that your personal data is an element of ad targeting in AI search. The privacy policy now makes that clear.

A Google spokesperson tells Ars that its privacy clarification does not indicate a change in how it handles your data with respect to its advertising partners. It’s not scanning your entire inbox to enhance your advertising profile, and it’s not giving any of this data to third parties. But if you pipe personal data into an AI search tool, the ads it shows you could be based on that information.

The core of the problem is that Google wants its products and services to talk to each other. Google sees that wealth of data as a key strength of its AI efforts. Some apps like Gmail are still given protected status in Google’s data handling, but there are now more avenues for that data to get out. The more data you share across Google’s ecosystem, the greater the risk to your privacy.

We’ve seen a similar exception in the way Google uses your AI interactions for model training . While Google says it doesn’t use personal data for AI training, it does use your inputs and the model outputs for that purpose. With Gemini integrated with so many services and connected to them via Personal Intelligence, those outputs may very well contain elements of your personal information. Google has said it tries to filter that content from the user activity controls, therefore keeping it out of training sets. However, it doesn’t promise it will always be successful.

Google is correct that Personal Intelligence is opt-in, but the company uses various prompts and pop-ups to entice users to turn it on without fully explaining the consequences. You may have turned it on without realizing.

If you want to ensure ads never use your personal data in this way, you’ll need to make sure Personal Intelligence is turned off. The easiest way is to access the Gemini settings for Personal Intelligence and disable the connected apps. These settings are also a few levels deep in your main Google account settings under Data & privacy > Personalization settings > Manage Personalized Recommendations in Search Services > Connected Content Apps. From there, you can disable connections to Workspace and Google Photos.

items.title: Spotify ramps up policy enforcement on family plans
paras: You home? Spotify ramps up policy enforcement on family plans If you share Spotify sub with family, you may need to scan QR code to prove it.

117 Spotify's logo and branding. Credit: Spotify Spotify's logo and branding. Credit: Spotify Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav As reported by Music Business Worldwide , Spotify appears to be stepping up enforcement of existing policies regarding Family and Duo subscription plans by requiring users to scan a QR code in person on the plan manager’s device in order to maintain access to it. Those who fail to scan the address verification QR code within seven days will see their account demoted to the free tier and be barred from joining any other Duo or Family plan for 12 months.

Spotify’s support documentation verifies the policy after users on Reddit began posting reports of receiving the QR prompt. The enforcement stems from Spotify’s requirement that family plan members reside at the same address—a seemingly reasonable policy in concept. But what if you have a child away in college, a spouse who works on the road, or any number of other circumstances that might see families separated by physical distance? The policy could extend beyond friend groups looking to save a buck, affecting actual families who thought they were using the program as intended.

Goldman Sachs analysts, in their October 15 Music in the Air: 10 Years On report, made available by HITS Daily Double , estimate that “a meaningful share of family plan users are not actual household members, but rather friends sharing a plan to reduce costs.” The report goes on to add, “We see additional monetization upside from tightening household verification on multi-user plans. Most family plans require members to reside at the same address, but enforcement has been minimal in practice.”

If the pressure on the accounts policy from Wall Street sounds familiar, it should. Streaming services have often turned a blind eye to account sharing during their growth periods, only to walk back the leniency once viewers are hooked. Netflix tweeted in March of 2017 that “ Love is sharing a password ” before launching its own enforcement policies in May of 2023 . Later that year, Netflix raised prices up to 17 percent , and by April of 2024, the company saw the policy pay off with 9.3 million added subscriptions and a 54 percent bump in operating income. Netflix isn’t alone in the practice, as competitors like Max (now HBO again) and Disney+/Hulu eventually followed suit with their own policy enforcement.

Goldman’s report argues that while family plans are great for getting subscribers onto the platform, “the per-user monetization of these plans materially lags individual plan pricing. In our view, these plans offer a greater value proposition to consumers than the standard individual tier, which we believe gives DSPs the opportunity to capture more value through higher pricing increases or by tightening the definition/eligibility of the family plan, without meaningfully impacting demand.” In short, analysts are confident that music streaming services such as Spotify can enforce strict account policies, raise prices, and still make more money.

So if you go to load up your favorite playlist on a shared account, you might soon be getting a warning that it’s time to check in with your plan manager. If that’s physically impossible to do within seven days, you might need to look into an alternative streaming service—or start digging through drawers until you find that old iPod.

items.title: A 1,000-mile cloud on Mars may reveal physics never seen in nature
paras: Cloud on the horizon A 1,000-mile cloud on Mars may reveal physics never seen in nature A new model suggests Mars may host ice-forming physics never directly observed before.

60 The cloud always forms near the Arsia Mons volcano before extending into a long, wispy strand. Credit: ESA The cloud always forms near the Arsia Mons volcano before extending into a long, wispy strand. Credit: ESA Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav Every morning during the Martian spring and summer, a thin and extremely long cloud emerges, only to disappear again. The wispy formation appears near the volcano Arsia Mons and gradually elongates until it reaches over 1,000 miles—about the distance from New York to Kansas City as the crow flies—before dissipating. This cycle then repeats for several months.

Since it was first recorded by a probe in 2018, scientists have been unable to find a plausible explanation for the existence of this cloud, often referred to as the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud (AMEC). Until now. Recently, researchers successfully modeled the cloud’s formation for the first time, their results suggesting that it may be driven by a physical process that has never been directly observed in any planet’s atmosphere.

“We found that we needed to include some exotic physics… physics that, while included in textbooks, is treated as theoretical and usually thought not to happen in nature. It certainly hasn’t been seen in action before,” Jorge Hernández-Bernal, a planetary scientist at Paris’ Sorbonne Université and lead author of the study, said in a press release . “Once we included this physics in our simulations, the AMEC emerged just as we hoped.”

On Earth, clouds usually form when water vapor creates droplets or ice crystals in the presence of tiny particles, such as dust or salt. The new study, published in Nature Geoscience , instead suggests AMEC could be forming through so-called homogeneous nucleation, where vapor changes directly into ice crystals on its own without any help from debris.
“It’s akin to droplets of condensation appearing in the middle of a room, rather than on a window,” Hernández-Bernal explained. “It’s wholly unexpected.”

This phenomenon requires extreme conditions—a sharp temperature drop of 30° Celsius within 10 minutes and high relative humidity. The Arsia Mons volcano also plays a key role. When wind current hits the 65,000-foot-tall volcano , it creates a powerful wave that launches moist air high in the atmosphere in a matter of minutes.

Scientists have assumed a similar phenomenon could occur in the upper atmospheres of other planets, including Venus and even Earth, but it has never been observed . That’s not too surprising given the extreme air humidity required for this phenomenon, which is more than 100,000 times greater than any value measured on Earth.

Before this modeling, it was not known that these humidity levels existed on Mars either. “We don’t have nearly as much information about Mars’ atmosphere as we do about Earth’s, so reproducing the AMEC to this degree is a big success,” said Hernández-Bernal, adding, “the result is remarkable.”
This story originally appeared on WIRED Czech Republic and Slovakia and has been translated from Czech.

items.title: October 26, 2006: The day Mary Pierce’s career was brought to an end by a horrifying injury
paras: Every day, Tennis Majors takes you back in time to one of the key moments in tennis history. On this day in 2006, Mary Pierce was taken off the court on a stretcher and would never return to compete on the Tour again

On this day, October 26, 2006, Mary Pierce suffered a horrifying injury while facing Vera Zvonareva in the second round of the WTA Linz Open. The two-time Grand Slam champion tore several knee ligaments, an injury that put an end to her career as she was never able to play on the professional circuit again.

Mary Pierce was born in 1975 in Montreal, Canada, but holding French citizenship from her mother, she chose to play for France. Pierce’s early career was impacted by her father’s violent behaviour, which in 1993 led the WTA to ban him from attending any tournament.
items.impact: After claiming four other tournaments in the next two years and reaching the quarter-finals at the 1993 Australian Open , she reached the final at Roland-Garros in 1994.

items.title: Alex Eala’s record against British tennis players as she prepares to play Mika Stojsavljevic in Japan
paras: Teenager Mika Stojsavljevic is about to compete in the biggest tournament of her career thus far. The British youngster, a former junior US Open champion , is set to play in the Pan Pacific Open for the first time in her career.

Stojsavljevic has been handed a blockbuster contest against Filipino star Alexandra Eala in the first round. Ahead of Eala’s contest against Stojsavljevic, let’s take a look back and see how the Filipina has fared against British opponents in the past.

Eala has played many of Great Britain’s most high-profile players in the past; most notably, Katie Boulter and Sonay Kartal. Will Alex Eala win a Grand Slam in 2027? Eala defeated Boulter – the former world number 23 – at the 2025 Hong Kong Open. Eala led the Briton 6-4, 2-1 when her opponent was forced to retire through injury.

Across a sensational summer, she reached the fourth round at Wimbledon, won her first WTA Tour-level title in Washington, and made it to the third round at the US Open. It marked a culmination of all of her hard work and was richly deserved.

Friendships are built by repeated contact, not by being liked
items.hook: This is the single most useful fact in the whole guide.
paras: Studies of primary-school classrooms found that children seated next to each other were far more likely to become friends than children seated across the room. When teachers changed the seating, new friendships formed with the new neighbours.

So the engine is: same place, same people, same activity, over and over. The day at the yo-yo bar followed by basketball is that engine working - shared activity changed how the other boy treated him. It was not luck.
items.do: Pick one activity he already likes and commit to it weekly for a full term.

items.title: Keep the proximity - change the watching
items.hook: Your instinct is half right, and the other half matters.
paras: You are right that being around the group matters: children nominate as friends the children they see and interact with most. 'Out of sight, out of mind' is real for acquaintances.

But guidance written for schools is blunt: merely remaining beside a group is not friendship. A child who hovers is read as a bystander rather than a player, and it holds him in the one-down position. Watching has a use - but only as the first twenty seconds of joining in, never as the endpoint.
items.do: Keep telling him to stay near the group. Add: 'then take a job in the game'.

items.title: Teach 'watch, then blend'
items.hook: The best way to join a game is not to ask.
paras: Most of us were told to walk up and say 'Can I play?' But that makes everyone stop and look at him, and makes 'no' very easy.

The better sequence, used by people who study play: watch for about twenty seconds to learn the game and where the line is, then slide into the action without stopping it. Take the end of the line. Stand in the outfield. Pick up the ball and pass it back.
items.do: Rehearse it at home in five minutes. Ask him to name the 'easiest job' in each game.

items.title: Host one friend at a time - this is the biggest lever you control
items.hook: The child who invites is rarely short of friends.
paras: Pick a child he has had fun with in the last month, not someone he admires from afar. Invite one person for one to two hours. Put away anything precious, have two activities ready, start with a snack, and let the guest choose sometimes.
Keep it short and end while they are both still enjoying it. Then leave a few weeks before inviting the same child again, so the invitation can come back to him.
items.do: Text one parent this week and set a date for the school holidays.

items.title: Ask the teacher one specific question
items.hook: Teachers see the playground. Ask them to name names.
paras: Ask two things: who does he play well with, and could he be seated near them or paired with them for group work?
Seating is one of the few levers that reliably creates new friendships, and it is invisible to the children - no one has to know it was arranged.
items.do: Email the teacher this week with those two questions.

items.title: Do not push into a group that is rejecting him
items.hook: Here the advice is the opposite of persistence.
paras: Where a group is actively excluding him, the guidance is to back off - when you back off from people, they can move towards you. Put his energy into two or three other children instead of one closed circle.
Friends in more than one place - school, a club, family friends - also make him far less vulnerable when one group turns cold.
items.do: Help him list three children outside the difficult group he could get to know.

items.title: One or two good friends is the goal - not popularity
paras: Kids need one or two good friends. You do not need to worry about him being the most popular child in the class.
His warmth and kindness are already the raw material. Treat this as coaching a skill, not fixing a fault - if he feels like a project, he will resist.
items.do: Say his strengths out loud, often. Confidence is what carries a child into a group.

items.title: Playing and talking with girls is normal and good
items.hook: Children believe gender matters far more than it actually does.
paras: In one large classroom experiment, simply seating boys and girls next to each other doubled how often they became friends.
Girls' play tends to build conversation, turn-taking and inventing games together; boys' play builds bigger, faster group play. Being good at both widens his circle.
items.do: No action needed. Just do not let him think it is odd.

items.title: When to get more help
items.hook: Ordinary friendship difficulty is not a disorder.
paras: Get more support if he becomes reluctant to go to school, is persistently distressed, has changes in sleep or appetite, or says it is happening all the time and he cannot make it stop.
Start with his teacher, then the school counsellor, then your GP for a referral. Kids Helpline is free and open 24/7 on 1800 55 1800, for children and for parents.
items.do: Save Kids Helpline in your phone: 1800 55 1800.
